question: What colour does copper turn when it undergoes corrosion over time?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Green**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **copper** objects are exposed to **moist air** for a long period, they lose their shiny brown surface and acquire a dull **green coating**.
 
• This green material is a mixture of **copper hydroxide** [Cu(OH)₂] and **copper carbonate** [CuCO₃], which is formed due to the reaction of copper with **oxygen**, **water**, and **carbon dioxide** in the atmosphere.
 
• The chemical reaction for this process is represented as: **2Cu + H₂O + CO₂ + O₂ → Cu(OH)₂ + CuCO₃**.
 
• This process is a type of **corrosion**. Unlike iron rust, this green layer, often called a **patina**, actually protects the underlying metal from further deep-seated corrosion.
 
• The **patina** forms naturally over time, usually taking **several years** to fully develop depending on the environmental conditions such as humidity and air pollution levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Statue of Liberty:**

 
 
• The most famous example of copper corrosion is the **Statue of Liberty** in **New York**.
 
• Originally made of **shining brown copper**, it turned entirely **green** by the year **1906**, roughly **20 years** after its dedication, due to exposure to the elements.
 
 
 
• **Corrosion of Other Metals:**
 
 
• **Iron:** Undergoes **rusting** when exposed to air and moisture, forming a **reddish-brown** flaky substance known as **hydrated ferric oxide**.
 
• **Silver:** Develops a **black** coating when exposed to air because it reacts with **sulphur** compounds to form **silver sulphide** (Ag₂S).
 
• **Aluminium:** Forms a thin, transparent layer of **aluminium oxide** which, like copper patina, protects the metal from further oxidation.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Corrosion:**
 
 
• Common methods to prevent corrosion include **galvanization** (coating with zinc), **electroplating**, **painting**, **oiling**, or **greasing**.
 
• Creating **alloys**, such as **stainless steel** (a mixture of iron, carbon, chromium, and nickel), is also an effective way to stop metals from corroding.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Corrosion:**
 
 
• **Reactivity:** Highly reactive metals like **sodium** and **potassium** corrode very quickly.
 
• **Presence of Electrolytes:** The presence of salt in water (like **seawater**) accelerates the rate of **electrochemical corrosion**.
 
• **Pollution:** Presence of oxides of **sulphur** and **nitrogen** in the air increases the acidity of moisture, speeding up the corrosion process.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Basic Copper Carbonate:** The specific chemical name for the green coating on copper is **basic copper carbonate**.
 
• **Reddish-Brown:** This is the **natural color** of pure, unoxidized copper. The option "Red" in the question refers to the initial state rather than the corroded state.
 
• **Aesthetic Uses:** In **architecture**, architects often use copper for roofing specifically because they desire the **green patina** look that develops over **decades**.
 
• **Environmental Indicator:** The speed at which copper turns green can be an indicator of **acid rain** or **industrial pollution** in a specific **location**.
